Cross-platform audit of the F2 fix branch — four axes. Verifier mode.

Preconditions (STOP and report if unmet): the fix + regression test are
COMMITTED on a branch (record its name and HEAD sha); the working tree has
no uncommitted changes to tracked files.

Allowed mutations: /tmp/xplat-test/** ; log/report files under scratch/hunt/ ;
`uv python install <version>` (uv-managed interpreters only) ;
`git worktree add/remove` rooted under /tmp/xplat-test/ plus `git worktree
prune` at cleanup. Forbidden: edits to tracked files; anything touching
.venv (inside the repo use --no-sync if you must run uv at all); git push;
shell profiles. All matrix runs use `uv run --no-project --python <V>
--with-editable <worktree> --with pytest` so no project environment is ever
consulted or mutated.

Step 0 — Host detection and setup
- uname -sm → Darwin arm64 = "M1 leg"; Linux x86_64 = "Codespace leg".
  Record which leg this run is. The other leg remains outstanding; say so
  in the report.
- git fetch upstream; record upstream/master HEAD.
- BASE = $(git merge-base upstream/master <fix-branch>). Create worktrees:
  /tmp/xplat-test/pre  at BASE  (pre-fix)
  /tmp/xplat-test/post at <fix-branch> (post-fix)
- Sanity: `git diff BASE..<fix-branch> --stat` → expected: exactly the fix
  file + the test file. Anything else: STOP, report the stray paths.

AXIS 4 — Enumerate the matrix we'll actually be judged by
- Parse .github/workflows/*.yml. For each job record: runs-on,
  python-version, notable env flags, and the test commands it runs. Write
  the table to scratch/hunt/ci_matrix.md.
- Flag specifically: every Python version CI uses; every macOS job; the
  process-replay job (mark RESIDUAL — it compares against upstream master
  inside their PR context and cannot be exercised before the PR exists).
- Derive VERSIONS = (CI's Python versions) ∪ {3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14}
  intersected with requires-python. `uv python install` any that are
  missing locally; record what was installed.

AXIS 3 — Backend axis killed by construction (static audit, pass/fail
per item, quote the offending line on any fail)
Read the regression test in the post worktree and verify:
  a. imports no Tensor/device/engine modules — only what
     deconstruct_function needs
  b. sets no env flags (no PCONTIG, no device vars) and creates no Tensors
  c. calls deconstruct_function (or the rebuilt function) directly
  d. the synthetic victim's missed global sits inside a genexpr-in-a-lambda
     (depth 2 on every supported Python — not a listcomp, which 3.12+
     inlines and would make the test vacuous there)
  e. assertions are membership-based ('NAME' in harvested globals /
     NameError raised), not exact-dict comparisons
  f. a short comment explains the genexpr choice
Also audit the fix diff: confined to the deconstruct_function harvest;
closure assert and TEST_PICKLE line untouched; no drive-by refactors.

AXIS 1 — Python-version matrix (the real platform axis)
For each V in VERSIONS, against EACH worktree (pre, post):
  1. Regression test:
     uv run --no-project --python V --with-editable <worktree> --with pytest \
       python -m pytest <post-worktree path to the test file> -q -k <test name>
     Expected: FAIL against pre (record the failure reason — it must be the
     intended miss, not a collection/import error), PASS against post.
     This must hold on EVERY V — that is the point of the genexpr victim.
  2. Harvest-delta audit: prefer Will's existing 832-callback walker from
     scratch/hunt/ if present (adapt invocation); if absent, write a small
     dump script in /tmp/xplat-test/ that imports tinygrad from the active
     worktree, walks all registered PatternMatcher callbacks, and emits
     JSON {callback: sorted(harvested global names)}. Run per (V, worktree);
     diff pre vs post per V.
     Expected: on 3.11, exactly one callback differs — remove_bufferize,
     gaining exactly {'AxisType'}; on 3.12+, empty delta (already inlined
     to depth 1). Any oth…[truncated for dataset]
Verifier mode. Checking the preconditions before anything else — they gate the entire protocol.
